tagline: Down the Bay's western shore to the old beach railway.
intro: Out of Annapolis, where the State House served as the nation's capital in 1783, the byway heads south down the western shore of the Chesapeake, by Edgewater on the South River, through Galesville and Deale to North Beach and Chesapeake Beach, once resorts for Baltimore and Washington, and on toward Huntingtown.
Along the way lie the forest, farmland and tidal marsh of the Smithsonian Environmental Research Center, where scientists study the coast.

moments.title: Historic London Town
moments.text: The brick tavern William Brown finished on the South River in 1764 served afterward as the county alms house, from 1828 until 1965.

moments.title: Galesville
moments.text: An early Quaker settlement on the West River, once the end of a steamship line to Annapolis and Baltimore, where the watermen's trade has given way to pleasure boats.

moments.title: Chesapeake Beach
moments.text: A Colorado railroad builder ran trains here from Washington to a resort of hotels, casinos and a boardwalk, until the last one left the 1898 station in 1935.
